Devlog.//_capture: Focus changes are pushed by the OS, not polled. These knobs control noise, not detection.
Devlog.//DebounceMilliseconds: How long a focus change must survive to be recorded. Discards alt-tab flicker and notification focus steals; a real file or app switch outlives it easily.
Devlog.//IdlePollSeconds: Only for noticing idle transitions and due heartbeats. Focus detection does not depend on this, which is why it can be slow.
Devlog.//HeartbeatMinutes: Max gap between rows while engaged. Bounds the span an unclean shutdown leaves open. 0 disables.
Devlog.//SuppressHeartbeatAfterIdleSeconds: Stop heartbeating once idle passes this. One row saying 'went idle' says everything; repeating it all night says nothing. Makes overnight and weekends nearly free.
Devlog.//_flush: Buffer in memory and write one transaction per batch - one fsync for many rows.
Devlog.//ExcludedProcesses: NEVER recorded - not recorded-then-filtered. With or without .exe. A placeholder row is written instead so the time gap stays visible without revealing content.
Devlog.//ExcludedTitlePatterns: Regex against the raw title, case-insensitive. An invalid pattern stops startup rather than silently failing to protect you.

Derivation.//_derivation: Every number here is a guess until a real workday exists to tune against - and that is fine. raw_event stores raw titles and raw idle measurements, so changing any of these costs one re-derivation, never a re-collection.
Derivation.//MinActivitySeconds: Activities shorter than this fold into their longer neighbour. Removes the residue that capture-time debouncing could not.
Derivation.//ExcursionSeconds: A detour shorter than this that returns to the same context counts as an interruption instead of ending the session. Without it, one glance at a browser splits a two-hour refactor in half.
Derivation.//SessionGapMinutes: Silence longer than this ends the session outright.
Derivation.//AwayIdleSeconds: Idle beyond this counts as absence. This is the ONLY thing idle time is used for: it cannot separate reading from typing, because scrolling is input.
Derivation.//CategoryOverrides: process -> category, overriding the builtin defaults. e.g. { "notepad": "Coding" }
Derivation.//_noise: Extra shell junk beyond the builtin list. NOT a privacy control - noise is filtered at derivation so the rules stay retunable; privacy exclusions live under Devlog.ExcludedProcesses and are never stored at all.

Git.//_git: Empty by default - real repo paths belong in appsettings.local.json (gitignored), never here. Scanning is on-demand only (--scan-git); it never runs inside the collector.
Git.//Repos: Array of { "path": "...", "project": "..." }. Two entries may share a project name - that is how two clones of one service combine into a single project's time and commits. Example: [{ "path": "C:\\dev\\myapp-api", "project": "myapp-api" }]
Git.//AuthorEmails: Extra identities beyond each repo's own user.email and the global config - for historical addresses, e.g. before an email change.
Git.//ScanLookbackDays: How far --scan-git looks back. Diff computation is the expensive part of a scan, so this bounds it rather than walking full history.
Git.//CommitAttachWindowMinutes: How far a commit may sit outside a session and still attach to it, so a commit made moments after the last recorded activity is not stranded as unattached.
